text:
maria: Customer reported duplicate + partial outputs when their client reconnects <1s after disconnect. They sometimes get a small chunk, then the full completion replayed. Possible double billing. Logs attached.

devin: Can you paste the client reconnect sequence and request headers? Are they using a resume token or just reconnecting and re-requesting?

maria: Logs (sanitized):
```
SSE: event: chunk
data: {seq:40, text: 'Hello'}

SSE: event: chunk
data: {seq:41, text: ', world'}

// client disconnect (network blip)
Client reconnect immediately:
SSE: event: resume
data: {session: "sess-13", token: "rtk-abc", last_seq: 41}

Then server emits:
SSE: event: chunk
data: {seq:41, text: ', world'}
SSE: event: chunk
data: {seq:42, text: ' full rest of completion...'}
```
No Idempotency-Key header from client. They also don't wait for close ack before opening new connection.

kyle: Hypothesis: race between resume handler and leftover queue for the previous connection. When resume is processed while the old outbound queue hasn't been fully drained/cleaned, the resume path replays cached prefix and the old session resumes tail -> overlapping seq 41 leading to duplicate content. Also possible billing double-count if token accounting increments on both paths.

jess: Can you repro in staging quickly? Try reproducing with a <100ms reconnect to mimic client. Also try adding an Idempotency-Key and see if behavior changes.

support-bot: Ticket CS-8472 created and linked to this thread. Customer notified.

maria: Quick repro script I used (node):
```
// connect -> receive seq 40,41 -> force close -> reconnect immediately with resume token
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Session: sess-13" http://staging.redwood/api/v1/stream
```
Observed same duplicate seq 41 + replay. Note: client didn't send any `Idempotency-Key`.

devin: Found code path: streaming resume requests currently ignore Idempotency-Key and we only dedupe at the completion-finalization step. That means an in-flight resume can cause a concurrent generation path. Pinging @runtime-bot to triage.

runtime-bot: Thanks for the report. We see the concurrent-resume acceptance path. Root cause: resume handler doesn't check for an active teardown lock on the previous session before reattaching. Working on patch to hold resume processing until the old session's close ack or cleanup completes. ETA ~24 hours for canary. Temporary mitigations: (1) clients should send an `Idempotency-Key` for the overall generation and for resume requests, (2) add a tiny reconnect jitter/backoff (>=200ms) to avoid the race, (3) server-side flag `x-reconnect-priority: strict` will force resume to wait until previous session is fully retired (we will enable for the affected customer as a canary).

kyle: We'll also add a unit + integration test covering: rapid reconnect + resume token reuse + billing accounting to avoid double-charges. Also adding a guard to avoid double-incrementing token counters for overlapping sessions.

jess: :thumbsup: Maria, can you attach the repro script & raw logs to CS-8472? I'll update the customer with the mitigations and expected patch window.

maria: Done — uploaded script + logs to CS-8472. Customer is willing to try the `x-reconnect-priority: strict` canary and add client-side jitter. Leaving thread open until patch is rolled out and billing audit completed.

runtime-bot: I'll post patch notes and canary rollout plan in CS-8472 once ready. Will also add telemetry to detect resumed sessions with overlapping seq ranges for retro billing checks.

maria: :eyes: thanks all, marking as actionable.
